To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the transcriptomes of evolved populations in complex environments are highly dynamic and diverse, 2) the genetic basis of the transcriptome diversity is related to the genomic background of the strains and to the selective forces, 3) parallel responses in the transcriptome are observed at the inter-population level, and 4) non-parallel responses are observed at the intraspecific level, indicating diversifying selection.

the adaptive response of Escherichia Coli to a fluctuating environment is dependent on the genomic background and that parallel responses are related to the number of mutations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the evolutionary dynamics of bacterial communities, and how they adapt to environmental conditions.
the evolutionary processes that lead to phenotypic diversity in bacteria and the role of environmental heterogeneity in the emergence of phenotypic innovations in complex environments.
the evolution of bacterial populations in a laboratory setting, with the goal of understanding the genetic basis and nature of adaptation in complex environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evolution of bacteria is not random, and that the evolutionary process is not a simple one-step process.
evolution of E. coli in complex environments is a dynamic process that depends on both genomic and environmental factors.
the adaptive response in complex environments is not only a matter of genetic mutations, but also of gene expression and phenotypic plasticity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how the genetic and transcriptomic changes are related to each other and how they are affected by the environmental conditions.

, the transcriptomic profiles of the evolved populations in this study were more similar to each other than to their ancestor, and that the genetic profiles were more similar within each population than to each other.
, by combining comparative transcriptomics and genomics, it is feasible to describe the adaptive responses of bacteria to complex environments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, although parallel evolution is the norm, there is still a large amount of variation that is due to the interaction between genotype and environment.
parallel responses are not only due to the action of a few key genes, but also to a number of genetic and transcriptional changes.

the evolutionary trajectories of bacteria in complex environments are highly dependent on the genetic background of the strains, and that the evolutionary responses of bacteria are not always predictable.
